title: Add regional scheduler + GPU SKU awareness for canary runs (tagging + routing)
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Motivation: We need the prod perf canary to (a) run in specific regions and (b) attribute results to fleet heterogeneity (GPU SKU) to avoid mixing A10/L4/H100/etc into a single time-series. This PR adds region-aware routing for canary requests plus GPU SKU tagging so dashboards and regression detectors can slice correctly.

What this PR does: Adds a simple regional scheduler to the runner that selects a target region (and corresponding inference endpoint) per workload entry. Adds GPU SKU awareness in two places: (1) a preflight "capabilities" call that resolves the GPU SKU for the selected target (or marks it unknown) and (2) propagation of gpu_sku + region tags into all emitted canary metrics/events. Adds config examples for us-east/eu-west and a default routing policy that keeps the canary small and deterministic.

Key details:
- New config fields:
  - workloads[].target.region (required): e.g. us-east, eu-west
  - workloads[].target.pool (optional): e.g. dedicated-canary (allows us to pin to a canary-safe queue/pool when available)
  - routing.endpoints_by_region: region -> baseURL
  - tagging.gpu_sku_source: "capabilities" (default) | "static" (for airgapped/private where capabilities endpoint may be blocked)
- Scheduler behavior:
  - Region selection is per-workload; no cross-region load balancing in v1 (keeps baselines stable).
  - Hard rate-limit is enforced per region to prevent accidental bursts (existing limiter is now keyed by region).
  - If region endpoint is down/unreachable, runner marks the run as skipped for that workload and emits a reason code (no silent failover).
- GPU SKU resolution:
  - Best-effort: fetches SKU from /v1/capabilities (cached for 10m per region endpoint).
  - If SKU can’t be resolved, emits gpu_sku=unknown and includes gpu_sku_resolution_error in the event payload.
  - Tagging is only attached to canary traffic; we do not change runtime-wide labeling behavior.
- Cardinality guardrails (per Telemetry guidance): gpu_sku is an allowed label only on the perf-canary metric namespace; values are normalized ("nvidia-h100-sxm", "nvidia-l4", "nvidia-a10g", "unknown") and any other value is coerced to "other".

Config examples (checked in under configs/examples):
- configs/examples/us-east.yaml: two workloads (streaming + non-streaming) against us-east endpoint, pool=canary-safe
- configs/examples/eu-west.yaml: same workloads against eu-west endpoint with static gpu_sku override (for early testing)

Testing:
- Unit tests for endpoint selection, per-region limiter keys, SKU normalization/coercion
- Integration-ish test with a fake capabilities server to validate caching + tag emission

Rollout notes: This unblocks phase 2 rollout (ENG-2851) where we expand from us-east to eu-west and explicitly validate that GPU SKU slice correctness prevents false positives from mixed fleets.

Checklist: [x] Config schema updated + docs [x] Tests added [x] CI green [x] Reviewed label/cardinality impact with Telemetry [x] SRE reviewed failure modes (skip vs failover)

Follow-ups: (1) Add a small "region health" panel to the dashboards so skipped runs are visible (ENG-2847). (2) Consider optional controlled failover for canary-only traffic once baselines are stable (TBD).
commits: perf-canary: add RegionTarget + endpoints_by_region config schema
runner: implement RegionalScheduler + per-region rate limiter keys
tagging: add gpu_sku resolver w/ 10m cache and normalization/coercion
metrics: propagate region + gpu_sku tags to run events and time-series
docs: add us-east/eu-west example configs and troubleshooting section
tests: fake capabilities server + normalization test cases
notable_snippets: Example config (excerpt): routing.endpoints_by_region: {us-east: https://api.us-east.redwood.example, eu-west: https://api.eu-west.redwood.example} workloads: - name: llama3-70b-streaming target: {region: us-east, pool: canary-safe}
GPU SKU normalization: lower-case, trim, map known aliases ("h100_sxm" -> "nvidia-h100-sxm"), else -> "other"
review_conversation:
Sofia Ivanova: Can you confirm we don’t do any implicit region failover? Mixing regions will blow up baseline comparisons.
Marcus Reed: Confirmed. If a region endpoint errors, we emit a skipped run with reason=endpoint_unreachable and do not reroute.

Logan Wright: +1 on splitting by gpu_sku, but please coerce unexpected SKU strings to a bounded set. Otherwise this will explode series cardinality when providers change naming.
Marcus Reed: Added normalization + coercion (unknown/other) and tests. Also limited tagging to perf-canary namespace only.

Thomas Baird: Can you key the limiter by region? Otherwise a temporary eu-west outage will cause us-east to back off more than necessary.
Marcus Reed: Updated limiter to (region, workload) bucket; added test.

Rafael Mendes: For oncall, we should include region in the emitted "run event" payload so incident-bot messages don’t require clicking through.
Marcus Reed: Added region + gpu_sku fields in run event payload; docs updated.

Felix Schneider: Example configs look good; could you add one with static gpu_sku for private deployments where capabilities isn’t reachable?
Marcus Reed: Added eu-west example using tagging.gpu_sku_source=static and tagging.static_gpu_sku=nvidia-l4.

Approvals: Sofia Ivanova approved after changes. Logan Wright approved with note to keep SKU mapping list in one file. Thomas Baird approved. Final approval from Rafael Mendes.
release_notes: perf-canary runner now supports per-workload regional routing and emits region + gpu_sku tags (normalized/coerced) for stable slicing in dashboards and regression detectors.
